newsitem.title: USA: Burnett shrugs off UAL loss, sees room for growth.
newsitem.headline: Burnett shrugs off UAL loss, sees room for growth.

text.p: Leo Burnett Co. is keeping a stiff upper lip, despite the loss on Friday of its 31-year advertising partner, UAL Corp.'s United Airlines.

"United's decision is obviously painful from an emotional standpoint. We've had a long and remarkable journey together," said William T. Lynch, Burnett president and ceo, in a statement after United said it had chosen Young & Rubicam and Fallon McElligott as its two agencies.
"We are in great shape from a financial standpoint," says Linda Wolf, president of Leo Burnett USA, in an interview. "We will aggressively go after more business."
Although she would not disclose what new business they're pursuing, she said,"We'd be foolish not to capitalize on our airline expertise."
So far this year Burnett has come close to replacing the $100 million in billings in lost on the United account with the new business it has landed,, Wolf says.

In breaking the news to Burnett's agency team of some 20 full-time employees, agency officials broke out a case of champaign and toasted the three decades of creative work it did, helping to build the world's largest airline, Wolf says.
Burnett created the "Come fly our friendly skies" theme for United and its trademark use of Gershwin's Rapsody in Blue.

Burnett account wins this year include business for Amoco; The New York Stock Exchange; Minute Maid's global assignment; Nintendo in the U.K.; United Biscuits in Romania and Bulgaria; Fiat in Caracas, Buenos Aires and India; a Kraft consolidation in the Middle East; United Distillers in Guatemala and Chile; Coca-Cola in Venezuela, China/Hong Kong and Egypt; Disney consumer products in Taiwan, and Walt Disney Co. in Singapore.

Burnett, which reported billings of $5.387 billion in 1995, currently works on five of the world's seven most valuable brands, as ranked by Financial World magazine: Procter & Gamble Co., Philip Morris Inc., General Motors Corp., Walt Disney Co., Grand Metropolitan, McDonald's Corp. and Kellogg Co.
